'''Cheuk-Yin Wong''' (born 1941) is a theoretical nuclear physicist at [[Oak Ridge National Laboratory]].<ref name=":0">{{Cite book |last=Wong |first=Cheuk-Yin |title=Introduction to high-energy heavy-ion collisions |date=1994 |publisher=World Scientific |isbn=978-981-02-0263-7 |location=Singapore New Jersey London [etc.]}}</ref>

Wong was born in China in 1941 and grew up in Hong Kong. He received his bachelor's degree in physics from [[Princeton University]] in 1961, followed by his M.A. in 1963 and PhD in Theoretical Physics in 1966 also from Princeton, where his thesis advisor was [[John Archibald Wheeler]]. Wong has worked at the Oak Ridge National Laboratory since 1966 and has held visiting positions at the [[Niels Bohr Institute]] (1968-1969), [[Massachusetts Institute of Technology]] (1982-1983), and the [[University of Tokyo]] (1988).<ref name=":1">{{Cite web |date=2024-07-20 |title=Cheuk-Yin Wong |url=https://orcid.org/0000-0001-8223-0659 |access-date=2026-05-18 |website=orcid.org}}</ref>

In 1978 Wong was made a fellow of the [[American Physical Society]] (APS) under their Division of Nuclear Physics Fellowship.<ref>{{Cite web |title=APS Fellows Archives |url=https://www.aps.org/funding-recognition/aps-fellowship |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260422155611/https://www.aps.org/funding-recognition/aps-fellowship |archive-date=2026-04-22 |access-date=2026-05-18 |website=American Physical Society}}</ref> He served as vice-chairman between 1997-1998 and chairman between 1999-2000 of the Overseas Chinese Physics Association (OCPA).<ref name=":1" /><ref>{{Cite web |title=OCPA - Officers |url=https://www.ocpaweb.org/home/page/officers |access-date=2026-05-18 |website=OCPA: International Organization of Chinese Physicists and Astronomers}}</ref> Wong was an editor of the journals ''[[Acta Physica Sinica|Chinese Physics]]'' from 1983-1989 and ''[[International Journal of Modern Physics|International Journal of Modern Physics E]]'' from 1998-2004. He is the author of the 1994 textbook ''Introduction to High-Energy Heavy-Ion Collisions''<ref name=":0" /> and, as of 2026, has over 200 scientific articles associated with his ORCID profile.<ref name=":1" />
